rationale: Data classes generate componentN(n) per property plus copy()/equals()/hashCode()/toString(). The phantom-injection routine exists in the analyzer but is never invoked AND reads modifiers from the wrong place (top-level instead of metadata). Wired and fixed, it must emit component1/component2 Method symbols scoped to the class (isPhantom), matching how Java's lombok phantoms work. M59 (#825) adds the two contract halves this fixture was missing: (a) EVERY synthesized member is contained by its class — the injector set ownerName for componentN but not for copy/equals/hashCode/toString, so on a real corpus file (JsonTestsData.kt) 7 componentN edges existed and 0 for the other four; (b) a synthesized name has NO navigable line, because its symbol range is the ENCLOSING CLASS's (3 here — `component1` is written nowhere in the 3-line file). The line is omitted, never guessed: unknown is a state, not a placeholder (#820/#821/#823). K1 (M60 kotlin deep review, 2026-09-27): these rows already pinned the LINE as null — the fixture knew the name was written nowhere — but not the CONFIDENCE, which stayed 1.0 on every one of them. So the certainty violation was unprotected: an edge naming a synthesised method at maximum confidence, indistinguishable from a declared member's edge except by knowing the isPhantom convention. The same defect java closed as JD-J13, in a branch that already computed isSynthetic and used it correctly for the line. Now pinned on `meta.inferred`, so the marker and the demotion cannot be removed independently. The declared member's edge is asserted WITHOUT the marker so the fix cannot be made by marking everything.
